audit.why: 52.08% over 1373 games - the largest sample in this slice - against a chart that concedes level 1 and the mid stages and gives Camille 2-3 and both item stages. A slightly favoured lane that opens badly into a rooting tank and improves once true damage exists is coherent, so nothing moved.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Bait the Q hook' and 'sidestep it' are the spine of the matchup and Dredge Line's cooldown is never given, nor is Titan's Wrath's or Depth Charge's. Without them 'take the trade and walk away' has no window.
audit.why: Dredge Line 14/13/12/11/10s, Titan's Wrath a flat 12s, Riptide 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s, Depth Charge 120/100/80s. The 14s on his hook at rank 1 is the whole trade window, and Titan's Wrath being a flat 12s at every rank is why the shield is always there for a short trade.
audit.corrected: spikes[0].text, early, mid and wants.foe[0] now carry Dredge Line's 14s and Titan's Wrath's flat 12s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors and one omission. (1) 'Your E gets answered by his point-and-click CC' - Dredge Line is a thrown anchor that can miss; only Depth Charge is targeted, and conflating them makes his engage sound unavoidable when the one that starts the chain is dodgeable. (2) Staggering Blow is described as rooting you 'on his first auto' with no mention that it is per-target and has to come back, so a player never learns that once it is spent the follow-up autos carry no CC. (3) Dredge Line also pulls Nautilus toward TERRAIN, which is an escape and a repositioning tool in a lane full of walls - it is never mentioned.
audit.why: Riot, Dredge Line: 'Nautilus hurls his anchor forward. Colliding with an enemy pulls them and Nautilus together... Colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus towards it.' Depth Charge: 'fires a shockwave into the earth that chases an opponent.' Staggering Blow: 'Nautilus' first Attack against a target deals increased physical damage and roots them briefly.'
audit.corrected: late now separates the dodgeable hook from the targeted ult, early and whys[0] state the passive root is a first-hit effect that must refresh, and mid names the terrain pull as his second use of Dredge Line.

edits.after: With Q up and a point in W you out-trade him: Q the double-tap for the bonus true damage, eat one Staggering Blow root, and W-slash the outer edge inside his 14s hook window.

edits.after: Staggering Blow roots you on his FIRST attack only and his tank base stats no-sell your single Level 1 ability — concede the opening wave.

edits.after: Land Dredge Line (14s) to cancel your E mid-dash and drag you under tower or into a gank

edits.before: Nautilus owns Level 1 — his Staggering-Blow passive roots you on his first auto and his tank base stats shrug off your one ability, so don't walk up to contest the opening wave. It flips at Level 2-3 once you have Q plus a point in W: Q's double-tap deals bonus true damage that ignores his armor, and W's outer edge chunks his max HP while healing you. The whole early game is dodging his Q hook (Dredge Line) — it's his only hard engage and the only way he lands a gank, so sidestep it and his kit becomes a slow-trading tank you out-DPS.
edits.after: Nautilus owns Level 1 — Staggering Blow roots you on his first attack and his tank base stats shrug off your one ability, so don't contest the opening wave; that root is a first-hit effect, so his follow-up autos carry no CC. It flips at Level 2-3 once you have Q plus a point in W: Q's double-tap deals bonus true damage that ignores his armor, and W's outer edge chunks his max HP while healing you. The early game is dodging Dredge Line (14s) — it is his only hard engage and the only way he lands a gank.

edits.before: Levels 3 to 6 are your cleanest window — bait the Q hook, then E in, W-pull the outer edge for the max-HP damage and heal, and Q-double-tap the true damage. His Titan's Wrath shield and sustain mean you won't delete him, so take the trade and walk away ahead on HP, not a kill. At 6 your R isolates him in the arena and cuts off his jungler, but he's a tank with a shield — treat the ult as a trade-winner and tower-dive setup, and respect that his R knockup off the passive root can chain-CC you out of your own dive.
edits.after: Levels 3 to 6 are your cleanest window — bait Dredge Line, then E in inside its 14s, W-pull the outer edge for the max-HP damage and heal, and Q-double-tap the true damage. Titan's Wrath is a flat 12s shield, so it is up for every short trade: take the exchange and walk away ahead on HP, not a kill. Remember he can also hook TERRAIN to pull himself out. At 6 your R isolates him in the arena and cuts off his jungler, but he is a tank with a shield — treat the ult as a trade-winner and dive setup, and respect Depth Charge chaining off the passive root.

edits.before: This is where it slips. Nautilus scales into a frontline that stacks armor and only needs one Q hook or R knockup to lock you for his carries — and your dive burst falls off as he piles on tank items. Your E gets answered by his point-and-click CC, so don't flank in expecting to delete a backliner; his job is to peel you off with the single-target knockup. Close the game on your first-item lead — take plates and roams off your Level 6 tempo — and don't let it drag into full-build teamfights where he out-CCs your engage.
edits.after: This is where it slips. Nautilus scales into a frontline that stacks armor and only needs one hook or knockup to lock you for his carries — and your dive burst falls off as he piles on tank items. Dredge Line is dodgeable, but Depth Charge is targeted and chases you, so don't flank in expecting to delete a backliner; his job is to peel you off. Close the game on your first-item lead — take plates and roams off your Level 6 tempo — and don't let it drag into full-build teamfights.

notes: The lane's central instruction is 'dodge his hook', and the late section quietly undermines it by calling his CC 'point-and-click' - Dredge Line is a thrown anchor that misses, Depth Charge is the targeted one. Keeping them separate is what tells a player which engage they can play around. Staggering Blow being a FIRST-attack root per target is the other missing detail: it makes his opening auto scary and his next three harmless, which is exactly the shape of the short trade this matchup wants you to take. Dredge Line's terrain pull never appears anywhere despite this being a lane fought next to walls. No fabricated ability names found in either layer for this pairing; the suspectNames hit on 'His Titan's Wrath' is a false positive.
